The '''1748 [[FLLA]] World Cup''' was the 20th edition of the [[FLLA World Cup]], the quadrennial international [[Arraby]] tournament contested by the senior men's national teams of the member associations of the [[FLLA]]. It was held in [[New Misos]] across [[Atirha]] and was won by the hosts, who defeated [[Seytinemas]] 4–3 in the final to claim their second FLLA World Cup title.

The 1748 edition is often described in subsequent FLLA literature as the "Greatest World Cup in History", a designation reflecting both the technical quality of the final and the high overall goal-per-match average across the 64 fixtures. The tournament's leading individual goalscorer was [[Emara|Emaran]] forward Halric Ostley, the first Emaran to win the FLLA Golden Boot; the prize was not won again by an Emaran until the [[1764 FLLA World Cup|1764 edition]], sixteen years later.

The 1748 World Cup was the last FLLA World Cup held in [[Atirha]] before the [[1764 FLLA World Cup|1764 edition]] in [[Raledria]].
